target: base builds from source / says wait for the catalog / uses a generic Nix overlay; skill (PR #22 guidance) produces the .flox/pkgs overrideAttrs workflow
prompt: The Flox catalog only has hello 2.12.1 but I need 2.12.2 right now for my project. How do I get the newer version through Flox without waiting for the catalog to update? Show the exact steps.
rubric: Correct answer overrides the existing recipe via a Nix-expression build: create `.flox/pkgs/<name>/default.nix` using `<pkg>.overrideAttrs` to bump `version`/`src`, run `flox build` (empty `hash = ""` -> paste the real hash), then `flox publish` so it installs anywhere. Mark INCORRECT if it builds hello from source manually outside Flox, tells the user to wait for the catalog, edits the catalog, or gives a generic nixpkgs-overlay answer that never uses `.flox/pkgs/` + `flox build`.

target: base (Jan-2026 cutoff) doesn't know flox run (shipped 2026-06-25); suggests flox activate -- or install-first. Skill (main, post-AI-441) produces flox run -p <pkg> -- <cmd>
prompt: I need to run a one-off command using a CLI tool (say jq) that isn't installed in my project or on my system. I don't want to install it into an environment or create a .flox directory just for this. What's the Flox way to run it once?
rubric: Correct answer uses `flox run -p jq -- jq ...` — run a command straight from a catalog package with no install and no .flox/. Mark INCORRECT if it says to `flox install` first, `flox activate -- <cmd>` (that needs an environment), or claims Flox can't do a one-off package run.
